solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Briefly stop seeing grotesque creature

indicators.note: said briefly, the phrase loses its final letter, as if cut short

parts.note: to stop seeing is to go blind

explanation.surface: An ugly monster vanishes from sight for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous, ugly sprite of folklore, a grotesque being.

clue.text: Pants Penny's wearing droop when pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up reverses the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to sag is to droop
P is penny plus the S of the possessive; wearing puts the other piece on top of these, as a hat is worn in a down clue

explanation.surface: Penny's trousers sag and get hitched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear but is the verb: breathes hard. 'wearing' puts the reversed droop on top of Penny's letters, as clothing is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant is to take short, quick breaths, which is to gasp.

clue.text: Great German workers' party nevertheless to be sold short

parts.note: a bee is a gathering of people working together, as in a sewing bee
tho is informal short spelling of though, meaning nevertheless

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to vend is to sell

explanation.surface: A German labour party is to be sold cheaply after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven, born in Bonn, is one of the greatest composers in history.

clue.text: Locals popular with Poles

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Residents are well liked by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' is the British word for neighbourhood pubs, not residents.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain one's local is the nearby pub; inns are pubs.

clue.text: Immediately report on friend's backsliding

indicators.note: the report comes on, i.e. after, the reversed friend
sliding backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: PAL'S, a friend's, written without the apostrophe
a report is a loud noise, a bang

explanation.surface: A tale-bearer reports at once on a friend who has lapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang is an informal adverb for suddenly or directly, at once.

clue.text: Descending onto platform, edge forward, increasingly

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes down on top of the second

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
a pier is a platform built out into water

explanation.surface: Stepping down onto a platform and moving nearer the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippy means cheeky or forward; lippier is more impudent.

clue.text: Dip in the cream pot

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the cream, the best
in snooker to pot a ball is to pocket it

explanation.surface: A finger dunked into a pot of cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' is slang for a thief who picks pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dip is old slang for a thief who steals from pockets.

clue.text: Piled up in the van, parking for days

indicators.note: parking takes the place of the days abbreviation

parts.note: in the van, the vanguard, means in front, ahead

explanation.surface: Luggage stacked in a van parked for several days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' means the front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aheap is an old adverb for in a heap, piled together.

clue.text: Port has aged with time, extremely rarely

indicators.note: rarely suggests an unusual, uncommon form, so the letters are rearranged
the outermost letters of time are taken

explanation.surface: A vintage port has matured, which is uncommon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the wine; it is a town on the Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town on the River Tyne, historically a shipping port.

clue.text: Tradition that mum's kept in the family?

definitions.text: Tradition that mum's kept in the family?

parts.words: Tradition that mum's kept in the family?
parts.note: mum here is silence, as in keeping mum, and the family is the Mafia

explanation.surface: A custom that mother maintains within her household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' means silent, not mother; 'family' is a Mafia clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Mafia code of silence towards authorities.

clue.text: Amount of money, including flyer, that's found in chest

indicators.note: the sum holds the bird within it

parts.note: an amount of money is a sum
a tern is a seabird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A sum of money and a bird turn up in a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a treasure box, but it is the body's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, located at the front of the human thorax.

clue.text: Aseptic fluid outstripping all others?

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A sterile liquid is better than every rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest runner, having most pace, leaves every rival behind.

clue.text: Endless things for tiller to do in London area

indicators.note: each of the two words has its final letter dropped

parts.note: a tiller of the soil may sow and hoe

explanation.surface: A gardener's chores never stop in a part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: SOW and HOE each lose their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, famous for nightlife.

clue.text: Bags of empty tweets

parts.note: to drain is to empty
birds' tweets are pipes

explanation.surface: Sacks full of hollow tweets on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is a noun for trousers here, not sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are narrow trousers; bags are loose trousers, both garment nouns.

clue.text: Marx died here, Engels also, strangely

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Karl Marx's partner Engels also died in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: Engels points to Karl Marx, but the Marx is Groucho, who died in that city.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx died in the Californian city in 1977.

clue.text: Be having seemingly penurious existence, as broadcaster is now?

definitions.meaning: to survive on nothing, as the very poor seem to
a broadcaster transmitting at this moment

explanation.surface: A poorly paid presenter scrapes by while transmitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of subsisting on nothing matches the studio phrase for being transmitted in real time.

clue.text: Cutter of large bristle — and second used to be cut

parts.note: an awn is a bristle on grasses like barley
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: with 'used' giving were, cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: used to be means were

explanation.surface: A large-bristled cutter, and a used one that has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to be' is read as WERE, and 'cut' then removes its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is a machine for cutting grass.

clue.text: Drop a little lower, keeping length in mind

indicators.note: with 'in', keeping something in means holding it inside
with 'keeping', places the length within the other word

parts.note: Latin cave! means beware, i.e. mind!

explanation.surface: Lowering something slightly while mindful of its length.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lower' is a cow, one that lows; its little one is a calf, and a cow drops it when it calves. CAVE is the schoolboy warning 'look out!'
explanation.definitionFit: To calve is for a cow to give birth, dropping its young calf.

clue.text: Inexpert way to collect rent in Bury

indicators.note: the outer pieces gather up the other word between them

parts.note: lay means not professional, inexpert
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rent, past tense of rend, means tore

explanation.surface: An amateur method of gathering rent in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay to rest is a euphemism for burying a body.

clue.text: No good going in without answer ready

indicators.note: the abbreviations for no and good are placed inside

parts.note: w/o is the written shorthand for without

explanation.surface: Something useless is put in place before the reply is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is a noun: ready money, cash. WONGA is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for cash; the readies are money to hand.

clue.text: Seeing much delight in always blocking editor

indicators.note: the combined letters stand in the way between the editor's two letters
the delight sits inside the word for always

parts.note: aye is an old word for always
glee is delight

explanation.surface: A sharp observer is perpetually thrilled at frustrating an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle-eyed person has keen sight and notices every detail.

clue.text: Endless, awful sameness, as a whole

indicators.note: awful means badly made, so the letters are scrambled
endless removes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Unending, dreadful monotony overall.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for all together, as one body.

clue.text: Spectators admitted crossing line, taking turn and turn about

indicators.note: the reversed line passes into the spectators' word

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators admitted to a match

indicators.note: taking a turn makes the letters face the other way

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: The crowd let in crossed the touchline, swapping places repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or spin round and round.

clue.text: Old military commander's memory not good, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An elderly general's recall is failing, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Montgomery led the British Eighth Army at El Alamein in the Second World War.

clue.text: Place lightning struck partly sent skyward

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending upwards reverses the letters
partly means only some of the letters are taken

explanation.surface: A location hit by a bolt from the sky, partly blasted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninth is a position, a place in an order of finishers.

clue.text: Filmgoer sees this game between Mike and Oscar

parts.words: Filmgoer sees this game between Mike and Oscar
parts.note: in the word FILMGOER the letter between M (Mike) and O (Oscar) is G, and the radio-alphabet name for that letter is a game

explanation.surface: A cinema fan watches a sport played between two friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike and Oscar are radio-alphabet names for M and O; in FILMGOER they flank G, which in that alphabet is called by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs on a course of holes.

clue.text: Suffered electrical failure, with potential to blow up?

definitions.meaning: an appliance ... when its fuse blew
a bomb is ... when fitted with a fuse

explanation.surface: An appliance broke down and might explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Fused covers both a blown circuit and a bomb fitted with a detonator.

clue.text: Irrational fifties remedy

parts.note: pi is an irrational number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty; two of them make fifties

explanation.surface: An unreasonable cure from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine, a remedy.

clue.text: Shellfish, stemlike, regularly appearing back on land

indicators.note: the reversed letters come on, after, the first word

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it

indicators.note: back means the selected letters are read in reverse
only every other letter appears

explanation.surface: Stalk-shaped molluscs keep turning up again on shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of stemlike give SELK, read backwards as KLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Winkles are small edible sea snails, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Something additional after the blink of an eye muscle

indicators.note: the additional item follows the other piece

parts.note: in a trice means in the blink of an eye
PS, a postscript, is something added

explanation.surface: An extra thing appears after a flicker of an eyelid muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: What a woman in R&D completely altered

indicators.note: the exclamation, a and woman are placed inside the two letters

parts.note: the letters R and D taken as written
eh? means what?
she is a woman

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a woman in research and development who changed everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wry: a rehash is a reworking, often one that changes little.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash is to rework or recast material into a new form.

clue.text: Played some groovy tunes?

parts.note: read once as performing music on a woodwind instrument, and once as describing something cut with grooves

explanation.surface: A musician performed some cool numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groovy' is not slang for cool here: it is literal, having grooves, as in fluted columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluted means both piped on a flute and grooved, as a channelled column is.
